questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Wolfe's four devices?
questions.explain: The nut graf belongs to the feature formula. Wolfe's four were scene-by-scene construction, full dialogue, third-person point of view and status details.

questions.q: A writer describes a senator's scuffed loafers, his secretary's nervous laugh and how he treats the waiter. Which device is this?
questions.explain: Status details are everyday signs of a person's place in society, or the place they want.

questions.q: Why did Wolfe say these techniques depended on 'saturation reporting'?
choices: Because editors paid by the word
Because only long, close reporting lets you write scenes, dialogue and thoughts honestly
Because it saturates the story with statistics
questions.explain: To write a scene, you have to have seen it or reconstructed it in detail.

questions.q: Why is the third-person point of view the most controversial device in journalism?
choices: It means stating what a real person was thinking, which is hard to verify
questions.explain: Even when based on interviews, reconstructed thoughts blur reporting and imagination.

questions.q: What was the problem with composite characters such as Gail Sheehy's 'Redpants'?
choices: Several real people were combined into one figure, which readers took to be a single real person
The piece used too much dialogue
It was written in the first person
questions.explain: Undisclosed composites mislead readers; today mainstream journalism treats them as unacceptable.

questions.q: A critic says New Journalism 'wasn't really new'. What's the best support for that claim?
choices: It was only practiced in Britain
Earlier writers, from Defoe and Dickens to Hersey and Lillian Ross, had used scene and dialogue in nonfiction
questions.explain: The techniques had precedents; what was new was the scale, the style and Wolfe's argument.

questions.q: Which writer is usually grouped with the New Journalists but writes in a first person that Wolfe's four devices don't really describe?
questions.explain: Didion's cool, personal essays, like Thompson's gonzo pieces, put the writer's own perspective at the center.

ideas: Readers' absorption in realist fiction comes from four devices, and a reporter can use every one of them.
The everyday signs of social status, such as clothes, furniture and manners, are the heart of realism.
Journalism had taken over the job the novel abandoned: showing how society actually lives.
